sasha: heads-up: saw a ~18% regression on small-batch decode with the paged-flash variant in a prod-sim run. KV cache was warm but token throughput dropped. anyone else seen this?

derek: can you paste the bench output / perf counters? which model, batch sizes, GPU?

sasha: quick paste from the microbench run (model=redwood-medium, A100 40GB, mem-opt on):
```
mode  kernel          batch  tokens/s  avg_latency_ms
prefill flash-merged   8      14500     12.8
prefill flash-paged    4      13800     13.9
decode  flash-paged    1      6100      23.4  <-- expected ~21.0
decode  flash-paged    2      11200     12.6
decode  fused-contig   1      7300      19.2
```
so decode@batch=1 with flash-paged is the offender (~18% slower than fused-contig / expected). KV hit rate ~98%.

maria: interesting — fused looks ok, so selector is choosing flash-paged for decode small batches. maybe heuristic tuned for prefill seq distribution. could be warp divergence or extra kernel launches for small batch + paged layout.

sasha: yeah i reproduced locally. prefill typically runs long seqs and picks prefill-optimized kernels; decode is short-step with continuous batching and the selector currently prefers paged to reduce memory pressure. suspect the paged layout introduces extra memcpy / page walking on decode path.

derek: can you run a nsight/profile with these flags and include counters for warp_serialize / l2_read_transactions / inst_executed? also capture kernel launch count. e.g.:
```
./perf/bench --mode=decode --model=redwood-medium --batches=1,2,4 --kv-probe --nvprof --counters=inst_executed,l2_read_transactions,warp_serialize
```

infra-bot: benchmark-runner: job 8732 finished — artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/8732 (flamegraphs + perf counters) :white_check_mark:

maria: looked at the flamegraph from that job — decode path spikes around `kv_page_manager::gather_pages` and several small memcpy kernels invoked between attention launches. kernel-launch overhead + mem copies add up for batch=1. also see increased l2 read transactions, likely random page reads.

sasha: so hypothesis: paged variant avoids memory blowup on prefill but for small-batch decode the page traverse overhead and extra kernel churn wins negatively. selector threshold should be adapted by path (prefill vs decode) and by observed kv-page-fragmentation.

derek: agreed. two action items: (1) add a microbench to perf suite that sweeps batch sizes 1..8 with kv fragmentation levels 0,0.25,0.5,0.75 for both prefill/decode and measure tokens/s + kernel_launch_count; (2) tweak selector to prefer fused-contig when batch<=2 OR when avg_kernel_launches_per_step> X. i'll own the perf test.

sasha: i'll prototype selector change and a patch that uses runtime counters (kernel_launches, memcpy_ns) to prefer fused for decode small-batch. will attach a reproducer in PR. pinging @maria for review on heuristics. :rocket:

maria: sounds good. also let's log a KV-probe metric from the serving runtime so we can correlate fragmentation to user traffic in prod (no PII). small batches are super common in chat loads.

sasha: yep. i'll include a lightweight runtime metric (kv_page_frag_ratio) + a perf dashboard. opening PR + perf run now.

derek: thanks — once PR is up i'll run the CI microbench and compare flamegraphs. :eyes:
